posts.text:
Your food bill went up. The shift ran long. Now you get to figure out why.

I’m building Never86’d for the operator wearing too many hats.

Here’s a sample demo. Made up records. Real calculations.

Start with one job.

Compare two sample invoices per pound.
Check a schedule against actual punches.
Calculate one pour.

The numbers stay next to the answer. Missing information stays missing.

An extra two hours needs an explanation. It does not tell you someone stole from you.

Review the source. Pick one next action. Draft the handoff.

That’s the loop I want an operator to understand in ten minutes.

This is the sample demo, not a live restaurant account.

Live AI, photo reading, account connections and the ChatGPT store release are still being built.

The planned offer: one location and one seat free. Extra manager seats paid.

Try the sample: DEMO_URL

Which job should we make easiest first: invoice prices, extra hours, drink costs, or the next shift?

I’m Myke, founder of Never86’d. I want the answer from people doing the work.
